metadata.title: Regional actors implement national strategies with limited flexibility for local adjustments.

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a country note describing governance arrangements in Chile’s adult skills system; it does not analyze student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/PIAAC) and therefore does not define a sampling frame, analytic sample, or survey-weight variables for estimation. The tables summarize responsibilities and expenditure structure across governance levels (national, regional, local) using OECD compilation and referenced institutional sources rather than survey-based assessment data. As a result, there is no basis to apply student weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) to produce achievement estimates. For any future empirical analysis using ILSA microdata, analysts should use the official ILSA sampling weights and replicate weights provided by the dataset documentation when estimating population-representative statistics.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because this is not an empirical assessment study predicting or scaling cognitive achievement outcomes from ILSA microdata. The note instead provides a governance mapping of institutions and responsibilities (strategy, intelligence, implementation, funding, delivery) across levels of government. Missing-data handling is not reported because there is no statistical model estimation on individual responses; the content is descriptive and based on institutional and OECD compilation sources.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used OECD compilation and referenced institutional sources to describe Chile’s adult skills governance structure; no student-level assessment dataset or analytic subsample is defined.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note describes how Chile’s adult skills system is governed across national, regional, and local levels. It characterises the system as largely centralised, with national ministries playing central roles in monitoring labour market trends, designing training strategies, and supporting implementation. Regional actors (e.g., provincial education departments, state technical training centres, and regional training councils) are described as implementing national strategies with limited flexibility for local adjustments, while local actors (e.g., municipal labour information offices and local public education services) provide job placement and adult education services in coordination with national agencies. The document uses responsibility-allocation tables (strategy, intelligence, implementation, funding, delivery) and an expenditure share at the subnational level to illustrate governance structure rather than reporting psychometric scaling or predictive performance metrics. No ILSA assessment administration, sampling design, plausible values, or missing-data procedures are part of the analysis.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a descriptive policy/governance report rather than an empirical large-scale assessment analysis. Consequently, fields required for ML/ILSA empirical estimation (e.g., student sample sizes, PV handling, missing-data handling, and model-based findings) are not populated because the document does not estimate statistical models on assessment responses. The sparse data fields reflect the report’s purpose: mapping institutional responsibilities and governance arrangements, not evaluating predictive accuracy or achievement benchmarks.
